items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The reason for bringing Hubert was that Bull Willimas had a dispute with Buchanan and took a poke at him... and he had Lloyd to fire Bull.

ctx.x: When Christmas of 1928 came, the Savoy management gave all its employees a gift of gold pieces. It was our first year as regular employees, so each received a five-dollar gold coin. The other employees, depending on the length of time they had worked there, received ten and twenty dollars in gold.

In January, Lloyd and Cecil wanted to bring Hubert Mann back into the orchestra, and we all chipped in to send Hubert his fare. The reason for bringing Hubert was that Bull Willimas had a dispute with Buchanan and took a poke at him, but missed, and some of the bouncers grabbed Bull to keep him from taking another kick at Buchanan, and he had Lloyd to fire Bull.

We took a banjo player named Teddy Bunn, until Hubert arrived from California, where it was said that he had been a member of a Holy Roly Church. Hubert arrived at the time that we were having rehearsal, with a straw hat, a light-weight suit, summer shoes, and no overcoat. Lloyd managed to get his tuxedo for the night, and when he came to work that night, he was so drunk that he went to sleep on the top of the piano, which was up, and he sat next to it, in a manner that made it easy for him to lay his head on and…
